Posted May 13, 2003
News and analysis by Richard Cowan

There are three stories for today. You make the connection.

First item:

Today's refugee hearings for Steve Tuck went very well.
See
 Tuck Refugee Hearings Begin. Canadian Government Brings In Heavy Artillery, Who Quickly Learn More Than They Wanted to Know. And I Play Lawyer. Special Report to MarijuanaNews by Richard Cowan

Even the prosecutor the lawyer for the Immigration Minister seemed moved by his story.

Much of the time was taken up by questions to Steve about the raids by Humboldt County law enforcement on his medical grows. They had repeatedly violated his rights under Prop 215, destroying over 1,500 plants, but they did not file charges against him until he filed charges against the sheriff and some of his deputies for violating his rights.

However, it was not until after he had given a very large quantity of medical cannabis seeds to Health Canada, that he was warned that his life was in danger and he had to flee to Canada. He placed his life in danger by moving this genetic material beyond the reach of those who would destroy it, because the suppression of medical cannabis is the highest priority for the DEAland government.

As I reported yesterday, the Canadian Justice Minister even sent a special representative to Steve's hearings.

Today, he showed up with a copy of an affidavit Steve recently gave to our friend John Conroy, QC about his gift of these seeds, so that Conroy can demonstrate that Health Canada has legally available medical cannabis to give to Michael Patriquen!
See
 The Slow Motion Murder of Michael Patriquen. Canada Really Does Have A Death Penalty, But Only for Medical Cannabis Patients. Breaking Their Own Laws To Follow the Prohibitionist Party Line.
and
 Canadian Supreme Court Hearings Could Make History, But They Are Only Good For A Joke In DEAland Media. Filed Under Oddly Enough. Dude, Is This Journalism?

Obviously, someone in the Canadian government knows what is going on, as is indicated by the next item.

Second item:

Evidence that the suppression of cannabis is the highest priority? Well, today, Martin Cauchon, the Canadian Justice minister, traveled to Washington, DC, to tell DEAland Attorney General the details of his new marijuana law before he told the Canadian people!

Canada thumbed its nose at the Bush regime over the war in Iraq, which logically would seem much more important, and has never demonstrated any concern about Washington's opinion on many other subjects. But he felt it necessary to grovel for approval of his new law before he tells the peasants back home what he is going to do.
See
 Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.

As it happens, his trip was widely derided in Canada. The following excerpt from a Canada Press story sums it up.

Excerpted Opposition Slams Liberals For Consulting US
By Jim Brown Canadian Press
Full story at http://www.cannabisnews.com/news/thread16282.shtml

Prime Minister Jean Chretien launched a campaign Tuesday to allay U.S. fears about marijuana decriminalization, but he succeeded only in provoking the wrath of opposition MPs who say he's letting the Bush administration make his policy.

The New Democrats, Conservatives and Bloc Quebecois all cried foul when they learned Justice Minister Martin Cauchon was headed for Washington to brief U.S. Attorney General John Ashcroft on the government's plans.

The problem, they said, was that the Americans were getting the inside dope before legislation reforming the pot law is tabled in Parliament.

" There goes Canadian sovereignty up in smoke, " complained NDP Leader Jack Layton. " Here's the American government advising on what Canadian policy will be before the House of Commons even has a look at it. It's quite astounding. "
(MarijuanaNews note: The NDP is a leftwing party. They say that they are in favor of legalization, but don't do anything about it.)

Conservative Leader Joe Clark agreed that Cauchon should have come to Parliament " before he went trotting off to the White House. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Clark supports decrim, but he is retiring.)
See
 Leader of Canadian Tories Supports " Decriminalization " Not " Legalization " -- Again. This Makes Mere " Decriminalization " a Defeat for Us. Defining Our Terms and Setting Our Goals.

Bloc Leader Gilles Duceppe wondered why it was so important to " obtain the permission of Washington " before taking legislative action.

Cauchon, meanwhile, wasn't about to tell Canadians what was said in the meeting with Ashcroft.

His office said the event was private and the minister would not discuss what the pair spoke about.

" The minister is presently in Washington, he's meeting Mr. Ashcroft in a private meeting and there's no media availability, " said spokeswoman Suzanne Thebarge.

The Liberals are expected to bring in legislation by next week that would make possession of 15 grams or less of pot a minor offence, something like a traffic violation.

Jails terms and criminal records for such offences would be eliminated and fines - possibly as little as $100 - would be imposed instead.

But government strategists say Cauchon will move at the same time to boost penalties for growers and traffickers. The government is also widely expected to announce new spending on drug prevention, education and treatment, all aimed at discouraging use, especially be young people.
(MarijuanaNews note: The devil is in the details. MarijuanaNews will have an analysis of the new law, when persons less exalted than Ashcroft are informed.)
See
 The Next Prime Minister of Canada Talks War On Us. Looming Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Proves Need for International Debate On Cannabis Prohibition.

Third Item:

When the facts catch up with the party line, change the spin. For the last several years MarijuanaNews has been almost alone in pointing out that the stories about BC Bud flooding into DEAland was nonsense.
From 1999 see
 Someone Floats A Rumor That DEAland Wants To Blacklist Canada;
Washington Denies Everything, But Canadian Prohibitionists Seem To Cheer,
Sort Of 3 Articles
and
 Canadian Police Lie to The Canadian Media Who Lie To Their Readers
To Justify More Power Over the Canadian People To Please DEAland Narks
An Utterly Wretched Piece Of Pseudo-journalism

From http://www.usdoj.gov/ndic/pubs/794/794p.pdf
Drug trafficking organizations in Mexico and Colombia produce an estimated

10,000 metric tons of marijuana yearly; approximately 7,500 metric tons of that marijuana is intended for U.S. markets.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) estimates that annual Canadian marijuana production is at least 800 metric tons, a considerable portion of which is consumed in Canada.

As the Canadians began to get nearer to actually doing something, newspapers started doing a little fact checking, a practice unknown in DEAland cannabis stories. Even the Canadian justice department has reportedly been doing the math. As MarijuanaNews has been saying, the volume of border seizures is the only hard data, and by that measure Canada supplies less than two percent of the volume from Mexico.
(From http://www.usdoj.gov/ndic/pubs/716/716p.pdf

The only concrete data that can provide insight, albeit limited, into marijuana availability are seizure statistics.)

From The RCMP http://www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/crimint/cultivation_e.htm
Smuggling of Canadian marihuana to the United States is rising. According to the U.S. Customs Service, 148 kilos of marihuana were seized along the British Columbia-Washington State border in 1994. Four years later, in 1998, the total stood at 1,182 kilos. In 1999, Customs officers seized 1,319 kilos. It is impossible to determine exactly what percentage of the marihuana grown in Canada is intended for the U.S. markets.

It should be underscored that despite the large quantities of Canadian marihuana smuggled into the United States, Canada is far from being the principal source. To put things in perspective, it is estimated that approximately three tons of Canadian marihuana are seized each year in the United States, while the exports from Mexico alone total thousands of tons annually. During the first half of 1999 alone, U.S. Customs intercepted 547 tonnes of marihuana being smuggled into the country from Mexico. The U.S. are basically their own main source of marihuana.

For a moment, those numbers were a problem for the narks, but someone came up with a great new spin.

Consider these excerpts from a Boston Globe story by Colin Nickerson, which also ran in the San Jose Mercury News at http://www.bayarea.com/mld/mercurynews/news/world/5830804.htm

In terms of tonnage, Canada accounts for only a small share of the marijuana smuggled into the United States. But in terms of value, some drug enforcement officials believe Canadian pot has surpassed Mexico's and Colombia's among US consumers because its high levels of tetrahydrocannabinol -- THC, the stuff that gives pot its pow -- commands much higher prices. In American cities, high-grade Canadian grass fetches more than $5,000 a pound, according to drug agencies.

But is Canada really the source of high THC weed in DEAland, or is most of the superweed domestically produced?

Consider this from the RCMP:
From http://www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/crimint/cultivation_e.htm

" Survey Results

The THC content of the 3,160 marihuana samples analyzed during the three-year period varies considerably. Although the highest value recorded was 25 percent, the yearly country-wide averages are much lower: 6 percent for 96-97, 5.5 percent for 97-98, and 5.7 percent for 98-99. In fact, almost a third of the samples were under 3 percent. "

On the other hand, the Mississippi testing results for the THC levels in contraband cannabis seizures, says that 14% of the cannabis tested in 2001 was over 9% THC.

From http://www.usdoj.gov/ndic/pubs3/3300/marijuan.htm
National Drug Threat Assessment 2003
January 2003

Mexico, Colombia, Canada, and Jamaica are considered the four primary source areas of foreign-produced marijuana available in the United States. According to DEA, Mexico is the source of most foreign-produced marijuana available in the United States. Mexico is also the only source area for which a statistically valid production estimate exists. In 2001 estimated net production of marijuana in Mexico was 7,400 metric tons, up from 7,000 metric tons in 2000. Northern Mexico accounted for almost 70 percent of the total crop in 2001

The overall potency of marijuana rose between 2000 and 2001, according to data from the Potency Monitoring Project. Average potency increased for all marijuana types (4.88% to 5.32%) and specifically for commercial-grade marijuana (4.69% to 5.03%) between 2000 and 2001, but decreased for sinsemilla (12.71% to 9.55%) during the same period. The average concentration of THC in submitted samples of sinsemilla has fluctuated over the last decade, ranging from a low of 5.77 percent in 1993 to a high of 13.38 percent in 1999. Nonetheless reporting from the Potency Monitoring Project indicates an increase in the prevalence of higher potency marijuana in samples submitted for testing. Marijuana samples testing at or greater than 9 percent THC accounted for 2.97 percent of samples submitted in 1992, 9.13 percent of samples submitted in 1997, and 15.29 percent of samples submitted in 2001.

It would appear that Canada could not even supply much of the high-grade market.

But so what if Canadian Bud was just two percent of what Mexico supplies, but was so expensive that it was worth more than all of the weed in Mexico? Why should the DEAland government care what rich Americans are spending on BC Bud, etc.?

I will be reporting more on this soon, but for now, connect the dots. It is not a pretty picture.

Also please see MarijuanaNews Still Needs Your Help. An Appeal From Richard Cowan.
